thread:
Alex: Heads-up — after rolling the mlx5 firmware + OFED package to eu-west-gpu pool last night we’re seeing a consistent ~55% drop in NCCL all-reduce throughput for 8xA100 jobs. Started ~01:15 UTC.
Priya: Ugh. Any errors in kernel/dmesg?
Alex: I grabbed dmesg and ib stats from one affected host. Looks like link flaps and some QP errors. Snippets below.
```
# dmesg | tail -n 40
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: 0000:03:00.0: mlx5_core: Warning: EQ overflow
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: mlx5_core: HCA health degraded: pmd:pmd-health
```

```
$ ibstat
CA 'mlx5_0'	: Active
    port 1:	state: Active
    phys-state: LinkUp
    QP errors: 12
```
Alex: Also ran ethtool -S on the mlx5 interface, TX pacing counters spiked.
Priya: Does NCCL fall back to the TCP transport or is it still trying ib? We should check NCCL debug output.
ML-Eng: From the ML side, we see collectives switching to NCCL_RING and much lower bandwidth; logs show `NET/IB` timeouts and retries.
Jamie: Could the new firmware have changed coalescing/pacing defaults? We saw a similar regression on a different fleet when firmware enabled HW traffic pacing.
Yang: I pulled package metadata — nodes got `mlnx-ofed-5.6-1` + `mlx5_fw_v1.39.2` via the auto-upgrade job. Rollout was staggered but completed at ~00:50 UTC.
Sasha: Any correlation with pod placement? Only cross-node multi-GPU jobs impacted, single-node fine.
Alex: Yep single-node looks okay. Multi-node allreduce is where NCCL throughput collapses.
Oncall: I throttled new job submissions to eu-west-gpu and pinched the rollout at 14/120 nodes.
Priya: Can someone run `modinfo mlx5_core` and `grep -i pace /sys/class/net/*/statistics -R` on an affected host and a healthy host?
Jamie: Also check `ibv_devinfo -v` for firmware version and `nvidia-smi topo -m` to confirm topology.
InfraBot: Deploy job 5123: halted by Oncall at 2026-03-17T01:02:30Z :warning:
Alex: Quick diff from two nodes attached:
```
# affected: /sys/class/net/ens5/statistics/tx_packets_paced = 1,245,312
# healthy:   /sys/class/net/ens5/statistics/tx_packets_paced = 8
```
Alex: That suggests HW pacing turned on aggressively.
Yang: I'm digging into the firmware release notes — there is a change in the default pacing algorithm that can interact badly with certain Linux kernel NIC drivers and cause microbursts to be throttled.
ML-Eng: ML jobs are timing out collective ops and retrying; cost is spiking and runs fail. We need mitigation fast.
Priya: Short-term mitigation options: 1) rollback firmware on a subset of nodes 2) set driver override to disable hw pacing (sysfs) 3) force NCCL to use RJ or TCP fallback (worse perf).
Sasha: Ops: I can roll back firmware on two hosts to validate. If that restores bandwidth, we can schedule wider rollback.
Oncall: Please label rollback test nodes `eu-west-test-mlx5` and block scheduling there.
Jamie: If we choose sysfs tweak, the path is under `/sys/class/net/<dev>/device/mlx5_core/tx_pacing_enable`? Need to confirm path/name — risky to change fleet-wide without testing.
Yang: I'll open an internal Jira with the firmware vendor and attach the logs. We should include `ib_read_bw` and `ib_write_bw` runs pre/post.
Alex: For immediate triage: Sasha — rollback two nodes. Yang — vendor ticket and escalation. Priya/Jamie — produce a safe sysfs knob we can toggle and test on the rollback nodes. ML-Eng — requeue one of the failing jobs to the rollback nodes once ready and capture NCCL debug.
Sasha: Starting rollback on host euw-gpu-029 now. ETA 18 mins.
Priya: I'll prepare a small ansible task to flip pacing knob if we confirm the exact sysfs key.
ML-Eng: Re-running a reduced 8x4 job on euw-gpu-029 after rollback would be ideal.
InfraBot: Alert: auto-upgrade job 5078 marked complete on 118 nodes at 2026-03-17T00:48:00Z.
Jamie: Also check kernel version differences — some nodes were on 5.15.0-101 while others already running 6.1.0-rc. The combination might be the trigger.
Alex: Agreed. Track kernel + firmware matrix in the Jira.
Yang: Filing vendor ticket now and pinging contacts — ticket #VND-3341. Included sample dmesg and ethtool counters.
Sasha: Rollback completed on euw-gpu-029. Running ib_read_bw now.
```
$ ib_read_bw
read_bw validation: average = 49.2 GB/s (expected ~75 GB/s)
```
Sasha: Hmm still low on single read_bw. Maybe we need to reboot after rollback or reflash properly.
Priya: Rebooted and retested; ib_read_bw shows 76GB/s after reboot and traffic pacing still low: tx_packets_paced = 12.
ML-Eng: Re-run on euw-gpu-029 with NCCL debug — allreduce throughput back to expected on that node group :tada:
Alex: Great — evidence points to firmware + kernel combo enabling HW pacing.
Oncall: I'll keep the deployment paused and schedule a controlled fleet rollback window.
Yang: Vendor replied acknowledging known interaction and proposed a patched firmware build. They asked for logs and sample host for remote reflash.
Jamie: Let's prep the rollback plan and a mitigations doc (sysfs knob + reboot) and communicate to platform users.
Priya: I'll draft the postmortem/blameless summary once we finish rollback.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here. :eyes:
